ANALYTICS_CONSENT.TITLE: May we measure how this site is used?
ANALYTICS_CONSENT.BODY: It shows us which steps are hard to use, so we fix the right ones. We collect usage statistics and record how the screen is used (mouse movement, clicks and scrolling) so a visit can be replayed afterwards. Your name, phone number, email address and seat number are never sent. You can decline and still book normally.

ANALYTICS_CONSENT.CONTROL_NOTE: Withdrawing takes effect immediately, with no need to reload the page, and on your next visit the analytics scripts are not loaded at all. Withdrawing stops collection from that point on; data collected before you withdrew cannot be recalled from the providers, and an item already queued may still be sent in the seconds after you withdraw. Either choice leaves searching, booking and payment working exactly the same.

GROUP.BOUNDARY_INTRO: One boundary drives both sections: it decides which refund rate a cancellation gets AND whether a reschedule pays a fee. It must be larger than both windows above, or the late rate and the late fee can never apply.

CANCEL_RESCHEDULE_POLICY_CONFIG.CANCEL_WINDOW_HOURS_HELPER: After this point a customer can no longer cancel. Enter 0 to allow cancelling right up to departure.
CANCEL_RESCHEDULE_POLICY_CONFIG.CANCEL_REFUND_RATE_EARLY_HELPER: Percentage refunded when the customer cancels earlier than the early/late boundary below.
CANCEL_RESCHEDULE_POLICY_CONFIG.CANCEL_REFUND_RATE_LATE_HELPER: Percentage refunded when the customer cancels at or after the early/late boundary. It cannot be higher than the early rate.
CANCEL_RESCHEDULE_POLICY_CONFIG.RESCHEDULE_WINDOW_HOURS_HELPER: After this point a customer can no longer move the trip. The same value also governs seat changes and stop changes. Enter 0 to allow it right up to departure.
CANCEL_RESCHEDULE_POLICY_CONFIG.RESCHEDULE_MAX_DAYS_AHEAD_HELPER: How far past the original departure date a customer may move the trip, in days.
CANCEL_RESCHEDULE_POLICY_CONFIG.RESCHEDULE_MAX_COUNT_HELPER: How many times one booking may be moved. Enter 0 for UNLIMITED (the default) — it does not mean 'no reschedules'.
CANCEL_RESCHEDULE_POLICY_CONFIG.RESCHEDULE_FEE_LATE_THB_HELPER: Flat fee charged when a reschedule is requested at or after the early/late boundary. Before the boundary there is no fee. Enter 0 for no fee at all.
CANCEL_RESCHEDULE_POLICY_CONFIG.EARLY_WINDOW_HOURS_HELPER: Earlier than this counts as early: the early refund rate applies and a reschedule pays no fee. At or after it counts as late.

COHERENCE.EARLY_ABOVE_CANCEL: The early/late boundary must be greater than the cancellation window, otherwise the late refund rate can never apply.
COHERENCE.EARLY_ABOVE_RESCHEDULE: The early/late boundary must be greater than the reschedule window, otherwise the late reschedule fee can never apply.
COHERENCE.EARLY_RATE_NOT_BELOW_LATE: The early refund rate must be at least the late refund rate — cancelling sooner may not refund less.

REFUND.TITLE: Refund Policy
REFUND.CONTENT_1: This page describes the cancellation and refund terms our system actually enforces. You can cancel a booking yourself from "My Bookings" — no documents to submit, no original ticket to hand in (our tickets are electronic), and no need to travel to an office. Before you confirm, the system always shows you the exact amount that booking will refund.
REFUND.RATES:
Refund rates when you cancel

  • Cancelled more than {{earlyWindowHours}} hours before departure — {{refundRateEarlyPercent}}% refunded
  • Cancelled between {{cancelWindowHours}} and {{earlyWindowHours}} hours before departure — {{refundRateLatePercent}}% refunded
  • Less than {{cancelWindowHours}} hours before departure — cancellation is closed and no refund is given

The part not refunded is the cancellation fee. The rates above apply to the amount still refundable on that booking, which may be less than what you originally paid if part of the booking has already been refunded.
REFUND.RATES_ERROR: The refund rates cannot be shown right now.
REFUND.CONTENT_2:
Where the money goes back

It depends on how you paid, and the system tells you before you confirm the cancellation.

  • Credit/debit cards and wallets — refunded automatically to the same method. How soon it appears depends on your card issuer or wallet provider.
  • PromptPay (QR) and bank transfer — these cannot be refunded automatically. During cancellation the system asks you for a bank account or PromptPay number, and our staff transfer the refund to it.
  • Cash — if the ticket is cancelled at the counter that sold it, our staff hand the cash back to you there and then. If we cancel the booking for you from the office instead, the money is still owed to you: our staff contact you for a bank account or PromptPay number and transfer it.
  • If a single booking was paid by more than one method, it is handled as a staff-processed refund as well.

We have no cash refund that you must travel to collect in person, and there is no deadline after which your right to the refund expires.
REFUND.MANUAL_TIMING: A refund our staff has to process by hand reaches you within {{manualRefundDueDays}} days of your cancellation. These are calendar days — weekends and public holidays included — because our counters operate every day.
REFUND.CONTENT_3:
When we cancel a trip

If we cancel a trip, that trip is refunded in full with no fee deducted. You do not have to cancel it yourself, and we notify you.

If only one leg of a round trip is cancelled, only that leg is refunded, the other leg remains valid for travel, and the booking's payment status shows it as partially refunded.

No-show

If you neither cancel within the times above nor board the trip you booked, the travel right is forfeited and no refund is given.

PRIVACY.TITLE: Privacy Policy
PRIVACY.CONTENT_1:
This notice explains how we collect, use, disclose and protect your personal data when you use our website, book a seat, send a parcel, contact us or travel with us, and it explains the rights you have under the Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019) and how to exercise them.

   This notice is published in Thai and English. Where the two versions differ, the Thai version prevails.
PRIVACY.CONTENT_2:
1. Who we are, and how to reach us

The data controller is N.J. Travel and Transport Limited Partnership, registration number 0203557004978, registered office at 3/5 Moo 3, Nong Chak Subdistrict, Ban Bueng District, Chon Buri 20170, Thailand.

For anything about your personal data or your rights, contact the managing partner by email at contact@nj-phuyaipu.com, by telephone on 08 1428 4492, or in person at the office above.

2. What we collect

  • Account details — your name, surname, email address, telephone number, password (stored as a one-way hash that cannot be turned back into your password) and a profile picture if you add one. If you sign in with Google, we receive your name and email address from Google.
  • Travel details — route, date and time, boarding and drop-off points, seat number, and passenger type (male passenger, female passenger, monk or nun), which you may leave blank and which we use for display only — it appears on your ticket, in your confirmation email, and in the booking list our staff see. It is not used to arrange seating, and it is not used to calculate any discount.
  • Payment details — amount, method, status and the reference issued by our payment provider. We do not store your card number in our systems. When you pay by card, the card details are entered on our page and sent directly to the payment provider.
  • Parcel details — the names and telephone numbers of the sender and the recipient, what is being sent, and the origin and destination.
  • What you tell us — the issues you report, your messages, and any images you attach.
  • Usage records — sign-in times, successful and failed sign-in attempts, and the actions taken in your account, kept for account security and for later investigation.
  • Data stored in your browser — see section 7.
  • Location — the site asks your browser for your position only when you press the button to find the nearest boarding point. That value is used on your own device to choose a stop; we do not send it to our systems and we do not store it. The coordinates our systems do store are the latest position of the vehicle, to show service status — not your position.

3. What we use it for, and on what legal basis

  • Providing the booking and parcel service, issuing tickets, taking payment, making refunds and contacting you about your own journey — performance of a contract (section 24(3)).
  • Verifying identity, sending one-time passcodes, preventing account takeover and keeping the system secure — legitimate interest (section 24(5)).
  • Producing accounting and tax records and meeting our obligations as a licensed transport operator — legal obligation (section 24(6)).
  • Tracking vehicle position for operational safety and to show service status to passengers — legitimate interest (section 24(5)).
  • Measuring how the website is used, and recording screen activity (mouse movement, clicks and scrolling) for later replay, so we can find which steps are hard to use and fix the right ones — your consent only (section 19). You may decline, and declining does not affect searching, booking or payment in any way.

We do not use your data for marketing and we do not send advertising messages. Everything we send you is about your own transaction — one-time passcodes, booking confirmations, schedule changes and receipts. If we ever begin sending promotional messages, we will ask for your consent separately first.

4. Other people's data you give us, and data we receive about you

When you book for someone else or send a parcel to someone else, you must have that person's permission before giving us their details, and the permission of a parent or guardian if they are under 16.

Conversely, if your details reached us because someone else booked a seat or sent a parcel for you, we received them from that person. We use them only as needed to deliver the service that was booked and for safety during the journey, on the basis of contract and legitimate interest — and you have the same rights under section 8 as a customer who contacted us directly.

5. Who we share it with, and whether it leaves Thailand

We do not sell your personal data. We disclose only what is necessary to the following categories of service provider, who process it on our instructions:

  • Payment service provider (in Thailand)
  • SMS delivery provider (in Thailand)
  • Email delivery provider (outside Thailand)
  • Vehicle tracking provider (in Thailand)
  • Cloud infrastructure and database providers (outside Thailand)
  • Sign-in and mapping provider, only when you use those features (outside Thailand)
  • Website analytics and screen-recording providers (outside Thailand) — only if you consent

Some of these providers are outside Thailand. Those transfers rely on the necessity of performing the contract you have with us, under section 28(3), and we send only what that service requires. You may ask us for the current list of providers in each category through the contact details in section 1.

We may also disclose data where the law requires it, where a competent authority orders it, or where it is necessary to establish or defend a legal claim.

We do not send passenger or parcel-recipient data to our accountants. What they receive is daily income and expenditure per vehicle, which carries no name, telephone number or journey detail of any individual.

6. How long we keep it

  • Your account — until you close it, and for 90 days afterwards.
  • Bookings, tickets, receipts and accounting records — 5 years from the end of the accounting year in which the transaction occurred. Our accounting year ends on 31 December (so a 2026 transaction is kept until 31 December 2031), as required by the Accounting Act B.E. 2543 and the Revenue Code.
  • Messages you send us — what you reported, the text you wrote and the images you attached. We keep them until the matter is closed, and 90 days after that we delete the attached images and remove the text you wrote. If a matter is never closed, we delete them two years after you sent it.
  • Usage records — 90 days.
  • Data-export audit records — 1 year. We record which member of staff exported which dataset and when, so that improper access to personal data can be traced after the fact. The search filters used for the export are erased after 90 days.
  • Vehicle position — our systems keep only the latest position of each vehicle, overwriting the previous one, so no route history exists in our systems.
  • Website usage statistics — held by the analytics providers for the periods they set. You may withdraw your consent at any time under section 8.

When you ask us to delete your data we act in two stages. First, we immediately delete or blank the details that identify you, such as name, email address and telephone number. Second, once the accounting retention period above has passed, we sever the link between the accounting records and the individual. Between those two stages the accounting records can still be traced back to you, as the law requires, so we do not describe the data in that period as anonymised.

7. Cookies and data stored in your browser

We set no cookies of our own. What our site keeps in your browser is:

  • Your sign-in state — token, username and role — until you sign out.
  • Display preferences such as language and theme, and the routes you searched most recently — until you clear site data.
  • Temporary values during a booking or payment — discarded when you close the tab.
  • Your answer about usage statistics — stored so we do not ask again, whether you accepted or declined.

The site collects usage statistics only when analytics is switched on AND you consent — both, not either. While analytics is not switched on, nothing is collected and no analytics cookie is set on your device, whatever you answer. When both are true, the analytics providers set additional cookies on your device: _ga and _ga_ followed by the measurement id (Google Analytics), _clck and _clsk (Microsoft Clarity), plus _cltk in the tab's temporary storage. That list comes from measuring the live page on 1 August 2026. Before you press accept, not one of them is on your device.

You can clear all of it from your browser settings, and while the site is collecting usage statistics you will find a withdraw button at the end of this page.

8. Your rights, and how to use them

As a data subject you have the right to:

  • Access your data and obtain a copy, including being told where we obtained it (section 30).
  • Have your data transferred to another controller (section 31).
  • Object to the collection, use or disclosure of your data (section 32).
  • Have your data erased or destroyed (section 33). You can close your account yourself on the My Account page, which removes the details that identify you; booking history and receipts are retained as accounting law requires — see section 6.
  • Have processing suspended (section 34).
  • Have your data corrected and kept up to date (sections 35 and 36). You can change your name, surname, telephone number and email address yourself on the My Account page.
  • Withdraw consent (section 19, paragraph five). For usage statistics, while the site is collecting, use the withdraw button at the end of this page (while analytics is not switched on there is no such button, because nothing is collected and there is no consent to withdraw). It takes effect immediately with no need to reload, and on your next visit the analytics scripts are not loaded at all. Withdrawing stops collection from that point on; it cannot recall data already sent, and it does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before it.
  • Lodge a complaint with the Personal Data Protection Committee's office if you believe we are not complying with the law (section 73).

Use the contact details in section 1. We will act within 30 days of receiving a complete request. Where a request is complex or involves a large volume of data we may extend that by up to a further 30 days, telling you and giving our reasons before the original deadline expires.

For security we may ask you to confirm your identity first, and to protect other people we may have to redact third-party details from the copy we send you. An electronic copy is free of charge.

9. How we protect your data

We maintain reasonable and appropriate measures, including storing passwords as one-way hashes, temporarily locking an account after repeated failed sign-ins, transmitting data over an encrypted connection (HTTPS), not storing payment card numbers in our systems, and limiting access to those who need it for their work.

10. Changes to this notice

This notice carries a version number and effective date at the top of the page. When we change it in substance we publish a new version with its effective date, and the next time you use the service you will be shown the change and asked to confirm your consent to the new version.

This notice does not yet cover in-vehicle camera recording. That section is being prepared and will be added in a future version.

PARCEL.TITLE: Parcel carriage terms
PARCEL.SCOPE:
1. Scope and definitions

In these terms, "the company" means the carrier, "the sender" means the person who consigns a parcel and pays the freight, and "the recipient" means the person the sender names to receive the parcel at the destination.

These terms apply only to consigned parcels that carry a freight charge of their own. They do not apply to baggage a passenger carries onto the bus, which is covered by the separate terms and conditions of service.

The company carries parcels between stops on its licensed routes only. There is no pickup from, or delivery to, a street address.
PARCEL.PROHIBITED_INTRO:
2. Items the company does not carry

The company does not carry the following.
PARCEL.PROHIBITED_EXTRA: This also covers cash, gold, gems, jewellery and comparable valuables, and strong-smelling food.
PARCEL.FALSE_DECLARATION: The sender is responsible for all damage arising from a false declaration about a parcel. If staff find a prohibited item during the intake check, the company refuses carriage and refunds the freight in full. If it is found after the parcel has departed, the company may stop the shipment and contact the sender to settle the matter case by case.
PARCEL.LIMITS:
3. Weight and size

A consigned parcel must weigh no more than {{maxWeightKg}} kg per item.

Baggage a passenger carries on board whose longest side is no more than {{carryOnFreeSizeMaxInch}} inches travels free, and at most {{carryOnFreeAisleMaxPerTrip}} such items per trip may stand in the aisle. An item whose longest side exceeds {{carryOnFreeSizeMaxInch}} inches takes up as much room as a seat and cannot stand in free floor space or in the aisle, so we assign it a seat and charge the fare for that seat over that leg. You may instead consign it as a parcel under these terms.
PARCEL.LIMITS_ERROR: The weight and size limits currently enforced could not be loaded. Please ask staff before consigning.
PARCEL.FREIGHT:
4. Freight, and what it does and does not include

The freight shown during consignment is the all-in price for carriage from the origin to the destination stop. It includes loading and unloading by company staff at no extra charge.

It does not include insurance against loss or damage, packing, or onward delivery to a street address. The company does not currently offer parcel insurance, and the sender packs the parcel themselves.
PARCEL.COLLECTION:
5. Collecting the parcel at the destination

When the parcel reaches the destination stop the company notifies the recipient by SMS on the number the sender gave, and the driver telephones the recipient before arriving.

The recipient must collect the parcel on the same day the bus reaches the destination stop per the timetable, presenting the collection code.

The company does not store parcels at stops, and therefore charges no storage fee.
PARCEL.LEFT_AT_STOP:
6. When nobody collects the parcel at the stop

If nobody is there to collect the parcel when the bus arrives, the driver leaves it at that stop and photographs it where it was left, as evidence. The system records the date and time it was left together with that photo.

Where the parcel was left is shown in that photo. The company does not designate a fixed drop point in advance, because stops differ; the recipient should look at the photo to find the parcel.

The sender and the recipient can see the photo and the time it was left on the parcel tracking page, using the tracking number printed on the waybill.

A stop is a public place with no company staff watching over it. Once the driver has left the parcel and recorded the photo, the risk to the parcel passes to the sender. The sender agreed to this at consignment, under clause 10.
PARCEL.CANCELLATION:
7. Cancellation and refund of freight

  • Before the parcel is loaded — the sender asks staff at a ticket counter to cancel and refund the freight (there is no self-service cancellation on the website).
  • Staff refuse carriage at the intake check — the company refunds the freight in full.
  • Nobody collects the parcel at the destination — the company has carried the parcel to the destination stop as agreed, so no freight is refunded.
PARCEL.LIABILITY:
8. The company's liability

The company is liable for loss of or damage to a parcel occurring during carriage in the amount of the loss the sender actually proves, but not more than 500 baht per parcel.

Proving the loss is the claimant's responsibility. The 500 baht is a ceiling, not an amount paid in every case.

The company is not liable in the following cases.

  • Force majeure.
  • Damage arising from the nature of the parcel itself.
  • Fault of the sender or the recipient, including packing unsuited to carriage.
  • Loss or damage occurring after the parcel was left at the stop under clause 6.
PARCEL.LIABILITY_TIERS:
Liability by type of parcel

  • Important documents, title deeds, contracts, vouchers — the company carries them but is not liable for their value.
  • Phones, computers, glassware and fragile goods — the company is liable only if the whole item is lost, not for damage to the goods, because the company did not pack them.
  • Food and perishables — the company is not liable for damage arising from the nature of the goods.

The company does not accept a declared value to raise the ceiling in this clause, and does not currently offer parcel insurance. A sender who wants cover above this ceiling should insure the parcel with an insurer directly, or use a carrier that offers such a service.
PARCEL.CLAIMS:
9. Making a claim

The sender must make a claim within 1 day of delivery being complete. "Delivery being complete" means whichever of these two events the system recorded first: the time the recipient collected the parcel, or the time the driver recorded the photo of the parcel left at the stop under clause 6. Both times are shown on the parcel tracking page.

The evidence required is the original waybill. The sender does not have to open the box in front of staff.

The sender is entitled to claim; the recipient may claim on their behalf if they present the original waybill. Claims are made at a company ticket counter (there is no online channel); staff at the destination counter decide them and pay in cash at the counter. If there is a dispute, the company will contact the claimant.

A claim under this clause does not affect the limitation period given by law.
PARCEL.CONSENT:
10. The sender's agreement

The sender signs the waybill to confirm they have read and accepted these terms, in particular clause 6 (leaving the parcel at the stop when nobody collects it) and clause 8 (limitation of liability). The waybill carries a short-form version of these terms and a QR code that opens the full version.
PARCEL.NOT_PASSENGER_BAGGAGE:
11. Passenger baggage is not a consigned parcel

The statement under "terms and conditions of service" about items the company refuses applies only to baggage a passenger carries onto the bus. It does not apply to consigned parcels, which are covered by these terms.
PARCEL.AMENDMENT:
12. Version and amendment

The version number and effective date of these terms are shown at the top of this page. The company may amend these terms and will publish the amended version on this same page.

HOW_TO_BOOK.TITLE: How to Book and Pay
HOW_TO_BOOK.INTRO: Booking your bus ticket is quick and completely online. Follow the steps below to reserve your seats and pay securely.
HOW_TO_BOOK.STEP_1: On the home page, select your origin, destination, and travel date, then search for available trips.
HOW_TO_BOOK.STEP_2: Choose a departure time from the list of available schedules.
HOW_TO_BOOK.STEP_3: Review the trip details and fare.
HOW_TO_BOOK.STEP_4: Enter the passenger information for each traveler. If the trip uses assigned seating, the seat map appears at this step.
HOW_TO_BOOK.STEP_5: Check your booking summary, then continue to payment.
HOW_TO_BOOK.PAYMENT_INTRO: At the payment step, choose one of the following secure payment methods:
HOW_TO_BOOK.PAYMENT_2: PromptPay — scan the QR code with your mobile banking app

HOW_TO_BOOK.TIP_1: Buses depart at the time shown on your ticket. If you arrive more than {{noShowCutoffMinutes}} minutes after that departure time, your ticket is recorded as a no-show.
HOW_TO_BOOK.TIP_2: If your trip is delayed, we will send you the new departure time by SMS and email, according to your notification settings.
HOW_TO_BOOK.TIP_3: Bring a valid photo ID that matches the passenger name on your ticket.
HOW_TO_BOOK.TIP_4: Keep your booking reference handy in case you need to contact support.
HOW_TO_BOOK.HELP_TEXT: If you have any questions about booking or payment, you can reach us through the contact channels listed in the footer of any page.
